extracted.intended_audience: devout Christians or readers seeking guidance in the interior/spiritual life (readers of devotional literature)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive devotional guidance (meditations) on the interior life: how to listen to God, cultivate love, humility, and perseverance, and accept suffering as participation in Christ's Cross.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embrace suffering as participation in Christ
rubrics_metrics.description: The faithful should prepare to carry the Cross, accept tribulations and sorrows, and even desire suffering to be conformable to Jesus crucified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose sufferings, regard them as consolations of great price; 'Buvez avec joie le calice du Sauveur'; accept adversities as the ordinary condition of this life and the remedy is to bear oneself. Suffering endured for Christ is preferable to worldly consolations and draws one nearer to Christ (citations: Rom. VIII, 18; Act., XIV, 21).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer suffering over consolations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regard the privation of consolations and tribulation as more spiritually profitable than the sweetness of consolations themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not seek to be exempt from trials; rejoice to be made conformable to Christ by suffering. Consolations are to be left to God's disposal; the soul should choose suffering when love for Christ demands it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate interior listening and solitude
rubrics_metrics.description: Happiness consists in hearing the Lord speak within: close the senses to externals, seek solitude, and attend to the inner voice of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer the interior voice to outward noise; 'ferme la porte de tes sens' to hear what the Lord says within. Jesus speaks in the desert and solitude, not in public places; prepare by daily exercises to understand heavenly secrets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Receive God's word inwardly with humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Listen to the Word not with human judgment but with deep humility and ardent love; accept it as 'spirit and life' rather than mere human sense.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely hearing the letter is insufficient — the Word must inwardly inflame and reform the life. Meditate, engrave the words in your heart, and obey them; hearing without obedience will judge the hearer (Joann., XII, 48).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct divine teaching to external instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: While prophets and teachers speak outwardly, God alone can penetrate the soul and make words effective; therefore one should pray for God to speak directly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask God to speak: 'Parlez, Seigneur, parce que votre serviteur écoute.' External instruction is useful but cannot make the heart inwardly fruitful without God's visitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renounce worldly attachments and seek the eternal
rubrics_metrics.description: Abandon love of the world and its transient goods; desire only the eternal and be detached from earthly pleasures, honors, and riches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The world is full of vain seductions; renounce it to attract the Spirit of God. Do not cling to pleasures or legitimate-seeming goods that distract from the life of faith and charity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make life a continual dying to self
rubrics_metrics.description: One's life should be a continual death to self: the more one dies to selfish desires, the more one truly lives for God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit to bear adversities for Christ; true spiritual comprehension requires submitting to losses and mortification of passions — this self-denial is the path to union with God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Walk before God in truth and simplicity
rubrics_metrics.description: Live with sincerity, truth, and simplicity of heart; truth liberates from calumny and seduction and preserves freedom of heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let truth instruct and defend; love eternal truth above all and be humble about personal merits. Avoid pretentious curiosity for divine secrets that neglects personal sanctity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine and confess in humility
rubrics_metrics.description: Constantly examine one's iniquities and be deeply remorseful for sins; confession and humility are necessary for progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not think oneself something because of occasional good works; consider one's infirmity and merit little, and subject oneself to penance and self-knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer God himself more than his gifts
rubrics_metrics.description: An enlightened love values the Lover more than the gifts received; one should rest in God rather than in consolations or charisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on transient tender feelings (consolations) as support — they pass. The true lover finds merit in resisting loss of consolation and in persevering in virtue through dryness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultivate a generous, sacrificial love
rubrics_metrics.description: Love should be generous, prompt, sincere, patient, faithful, humble, obedient, chaste, and magnanimous; it must be ready to give all for God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Love makes heavy things light and enables great undertakings; it overflows, exhausts itself in praise, and is constant even amid trials. The list of charity's qualities (prompt, prudent, patient, etc.) describes the moral formation sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be ready to renounce consolations and endure privation
rubrics_metrics.description: Progress in the spiritual life is marked not by abundance of consolations but by the capacity to bear their privation with humility and perseverance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue daily practices even in dryness and avoid abandoning exercises because of lack of feeling. The ability to accept privation purifies and strengthens the soul.

rubrics_metrics.name: Persevere in trials and resist temptation steadfastly
rubrics_metrics.description: True love remains firm in temptation and adversity; do not abandon a work at the first contradiction or seek consolation when trials come.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combat temptations like a courageous soldier; if you fall through weakness, rise humbly with renewed courage and dependence on grace. Resist the devil's suggestions and reject shameful or criminal thoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject proud curiosity about divine mysteries
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid presumptuous curiosity to pry into God's secrets; it often leads to temptation and falls if it replaces attention to personal salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer concern for one's own salvation and the mortification of passions to speculative desire for hidden things; curiosity breeds pride and leads away from union with God.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice discernment between outward acts and inward fruit
rubrics_metrics.description: External observances (books, images, signs, liturgical marks) are insufficient if not accompanied by interior purification and attention to God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some persons have external devotions but lack interior life; the soul enlightened by the Spirit desires what is eternal and is detached from outward vanities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust God's promises and remain faithful to the end
rubrics_metrics.description: God rewards the faithful and keeps his promises; perseverance in love and fidelity until the end is necessary for salvation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: God will give what he promised, but one must remain in love and fidelity. 'Ce que j'ai promis, je le donnerai' — stay faithful, for rewards follow perseverance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to interior promptings by prayer and reform
rubrics_metrics.description: When God speaks inwardly, respond by prayer, conversion, and reformation of life; accept both correction and consolation as lessons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: God visits by temptation and consolation to teach and to urge virtue: allow those visits to instruct, reform, and increase perseverance rather than merely seeking consolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal spiritual favors with humility
rubrics_metrics.description: When graces and movements of piety are experienced, keep them hidden, speak little of them, and beware of pride in such favors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exaggerate the greatness of one's graces; remain poor in spirit and fear a favor that may pass. Progress is not in enjoying consolations but in bearing their loss without abandoning practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arm oneself with faith and the sign of the Cross against fear
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith and being marked with the Cross protect from fear of demons and spiritual attacks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If armed with faith and marked by Christ's Cross, one need not fear even demonic enemies; rely upon faith as spiritual armor.
